```markdown
[Date]

Ambetter (WellCare)
Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-07**
- **Member:** Jordan Foster
- **Member ID:** W794852405
- **Reference number:** POC-EE22487639-86426
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Governing policy:** Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf (Date of Last Revision: 04/25)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-07 states that the records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file document the conservative care the plan's own policy asks for. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have set out the plan's published criteria, quoted exactly from Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114), next to what my medical records show.

## The plan's criteria and my records

**The policy states:**

> "discectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following:"

**1. The policy requires:**

> "Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc;"

**My records show:** MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-06-28 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion.

**2. The policy requires:**

> "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

**My records show:** the same MRI of 2026-06-28 shows severe right lateral recess stenosis with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. Nerve root compression is therefore confirmed by imaging, at a specific level and side.

**3. One of the qualifying findings the policy lists is:**

> "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

**My records show:** radicular pain into my right calf, a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, and positive provocative testing on the affected side. My symptoms have lasted 12 months and are progressive, and rest does not relieve them. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.

## The conservative care the plan asks for

The denial rests on conservative treatment, so I want to address that point directly against the plan's own list. The policy states:

> "Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following:"

**a) The policy requires:**

> "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

**My records show:** supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 10 weeks, from 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Ten weeks is more than twice the four weeks the policy requires, and it is within the last year.

**b) The policy requires:**

> "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification;"

**My records show:** [please complete from the chart — dates and description of documented activity modification, e.g. the physician office notes or physical therapy records describing restrictions on standing, lifting or work duties]. I am asking that this documentation be reviewed as part of my appeal.

**1) The policy requires:**

> "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

**My records show:** NSAIDs taken for 6 months with inadequate relief. That is far longer than the three weeks the policy sets as the threshold.

**2) The policy lists:**

> "2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

**My records show:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. [Please confirm from the procedure note whether this injection is documented as an epidural steroid injection, and include that note with this appeal.]

Taken together, the file documents 12 months of progressive symptoms, 16 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks, six months of NSAIDs, and a steroid injection that gave three weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned. These are the same treatments the plan's policy lists, tried in the timeframe the policy sets, and they did not resolve my condition.

## A note on the other criteria in the policy

The policy also contains a separate pathway based on motor findings, including:

> "R adiculopathy with motor deficit and one of the following:"

> "Severe weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by:"

> "a score of ≤ 3 on the Me dical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale, or the inability to ambulate;"

> "Mild to moderate weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by a score of 4 on the Medical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale and one of the following:"

> "Worsening weakness or motor deficit;"

My records describe a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level but do not state a Medical Research Council muscle strength score. I am relying on the sensory-deficit pathway quoted above. If the reviewer would like strength grading documented, my surgeon's office can be asked to supply it: [contact for Dr. Reyes' office].

## What I am asking for

I am asking Ambetter (WellCare) to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies which specific criterion in Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) the plan finds unmet, and which document in my file was reviewed in reaching that conclusion. I also ask that all of the records listed above — the MRI report of 2026-06-28, the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, the injection record of 2026-06-09, and my medication history — be included in the review.

Please also let me know if I have the right to a further review, including an external review, if this appeal is not decided in my favor.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, by **2027-02-03**. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial notice. I understand appeals may also be submitted online at ambetterhealth.com by selecting North Carolina and using that state's appeal or grievance form, or by calling the number on my member ID card. My denial letter is the authoritative source for the address and deadline.

Thank you for taking the time to review my case again.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Foster**
Member ID: W794852405
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone]
[Email]
Date: [Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-07 (Reference POC-EE22487639-86426)
- MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-06-28
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12 (16 visits)
- Injection record, 2026-06-09
- [Office notes documenting activity modification]
- [Any additional records from Dr. Reyes' office]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```
